subject: Day 39: football-hold tummy time
bodyText:
Today's focus
Tummy time is the prescribed counterweight to back-sleeping, but floor sessions often draw protest at 6-10 weeks. Today is a lower-effort variant that keeps prone time accruing when the floor is a fight.

Action items
- Drape Avi across your forearm in a football hold as a low-protest tummy-time substitute when floor time turns fussy; it still loads the neck and upper body and counts toward the daily total. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Keep limiting container time (bouncer, swing, car seat outside the car) to under two hours a day so floor and prone practice is not crowded out. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is on the calendar; with Anoushka's postpartum visit landing this week, lock both appointments in together while the schedule is open. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hating floor tummy time at 6-10 weeks is normal; shorten the bouts and pair them with your face or a song rather than dropping the practice.
- [monitor] A head tilt that responds to repositioning is low-grade, but a tilt that persists despite varying his held and sleep positions warrants a mention at the 2-month visit.
- [monitor] Forceful arching or painful, frequent spit-up during feeds; track it and raise reflux or milk-protein intolerance at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24h or refusal of several feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, blue lips, limpness, or asymmetric movement on one side: call same-day, and dial 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

Enrichment opportunities
- Use the forearm football hold and across-the-lap incline as gentler tummy-time variants; rotating positions keeps prone time accumulating toward 30 minutes a day even on protest-heavy days. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take coo turns: when Avi vocalizes, respond as if he spoke, pause, wait for his next sound, then respond again. These proto-conversations are the serve-and-return pattern linked to stronger later language. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Slowly track a high-contrast card across his full visual field, side to side; by now he can follow an object roughly 180 degrees, and this exercises smooth visual pursuit. AAP HealthyChildren baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 41 (this week): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit with the first vaccine round (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).
- Day 57-72: expect 24-48h of post-vaccine fussiness, low-grade fever, and drowsiness.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
